timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: IoT devices are everywhere now. What's the risk?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Billions of constrained, unpatched devices with default credentials. Each one a door.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do we give devices an identity?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Unique certificates or keys at manufacture. Per-device keys, not one shared secret.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Secure boot and signed firmware. Only verified code runs and updates.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Encrypt it. TLS or DTLS over MQTT or CoAP. Never plaintext.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: No. Route through gateways so devices never publish services to the internet.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Force a change on first boot. Default credentials are how most IoT gets owned.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Segment IoT from corporate IT. A hacked sensor should not reach the file server.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Watch device telemetry for anomalies. Odd traffic from a sensor is a red flag.
